The final answer of 29 is correct, but the proposed reasoning is not valid. The transparent-position sets are misread (for example, the front-face list gives the '-' positions as transparent) and the inclusion-exclusion counts don't follow from the constraints.

Reading '+' as red letter pixels and '-' as transparent background, each '-' sight line must be entirely transparent, and each '+' sight line needs at least one red cube. The lines forced transparent by the '-' pixels cover 109 cubes, leaving 16 candidates. But the top-face '-' lines at x=3 and x=1 are not all covered, and the candidate set is not the right one. Recounting carefully: at height z≤3 only the cubes with x=2 and y∈{0,2,4} stay free (12 cubes), and at z=4 every cube not on the eight top-face '-' columns stays free (17 cubes). That gives 29 free cubes. Every '+' line contains at least one of them, so 29 is achievable, and it is the maximum because the other 96 cubes are forced transparent. The result also holds under the mirror-image orientation of the top face.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
CONFIDENCE: 3
